source: BV NR467 Pt B, Ch 4 Sec 3, Table 1 — corrosion addition for one side of a structural member (July 2026, page 133), read from the page image.
note: ONE table for the whole app. Each of the five source workbooks abridged this table its own way and three of them disagreed with the rule; see `divergesFromWorkbooks` below. Values are the addition for ONE SIDE: a plate takes tc1 + tc2 + t_res, one entry per face.

entries.label: Ballast water tank, bilge tank, drain storage tank, chain locker
entries.notes: Excludes cargo oil tanks that may carry ballast under MARPOL 73/78 Reg 18. Add 1,0 mm to the plate surface within 3 m above the chain locker bottom.

entries.label: Cargo oil tank, fuel and lube oil tank
entries.notes: Also chemical tanker cargo tanks, fuel chemical tanks and METHANOLFUEL / ETHANOLFUEL tanks. tc may be taken as 0 for tanks with a protective lining or coating.

entries.label: Liquefied gas tank
entries.notes: Applied when required by Pt D Ch 9 Sec 4 [2.1.5] or NR529 Ch 3 Sec 2 [1].

entries.label: Dry bulk cargo hold — general
entries.notes: Includes all structural members and areas within cargo holds of a cement carrier.

entries.label: Dry bulk cargo hold — inner bottom, single-hull side, double-hull inner side, transverse bulkhead and sloping stool plating
Dry bulk cargo hold — frames, ordinary stiffeners and primary supporting members
entries.notes: Add 0,50 mm within 3 m above the bottom of the hold.

entries.label: Tanks for water-based or oil-based process muds or brines
Compartment between independent tank and inner side — asphalt carrier
Cofferdam or void space
entries.notes: Includes cofferdams and spaces adjacent to membrane or independent tanks of a liquefied gas carrier, and spaces around a gasfuel tank. May be taken as 0 with environmental control such as inerting. For the outer shell plating a pipe tunnel counts as a ballast water tank.

entries.label: Dry spaces — machinery space, pump room, store rooms, steering gear space, passageways
entries.notes: For the Ch 8 Sec 1 direct strength assessment of a container ship, tc1 or tc2 is taken as 0,0 mm.

divergesFromWorkbooks.comment: The fore and aft workbooks carry a 'weather deck exposed' entry at 1,7 mm. The rule has no such one-side addition — a weather deck is 'exposed to atmosphere' at 1,00 on its upper face, and the second face is whatever the space below is. 1,7 looks like a pre-combined figure used as if it were a one-side value.
